Raspberry Pi3 Description: Everyone knows and loves Raspberry Pi3, but what if you didn’t need additional peripherals to make it wireless. The Raspberry Pi3 is here to provide you with the same Pi as before but now with double the ram and a much faster processor. The credit-card sized computer is capable of many of the things that your desktop PC does, like spreadsheets, word-processing and playing high-definition video and games. It can run several flavors of Linux (and even Windows 10 free-of-charge) and is being used to teach kids all over the world how to program…

The secret sauce that makes this computer so small and powerful is the Broadcom BCM2837, an ARM Cortex-A53 64bit Quad Core Processor System-on-Chip. The GPU provides Open GL ES 2.0, hardware-accelerated OpenVG, and 1080p30 H.264 high-profile decode and is capable of 1Gpixel/s, 1.5Gtexel/s or 24 GFLOPs of general purpose compute. What’s that all mean? It means that if you plug the Raspberry Pi3 into your HDTV, you could watch BluRay quality video, using H.264 at 40MBits/s.

The biggest change that has been enacted with the Raspberry Pi3 is an upgrade to a next generation main processor and improved connectivity with Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and BCM43143 WiFi on board. Additionally, the Raspberry Pi 3 has improved power management, with an upgraded switched power source up to 2.5 Amps, to support more powerful external USB devices.

The Raspberry Pi3’s four built-in USB ports provide enough connectivity for a mouse, keyboard, or anything else that you feel the RPi needs, but if you want to add even more you can still use a USB hub. Keep in mind, it is recommended that you use a powered hub so as not to overtax the on-board voltage regulator. Powering the Raspberry Pi3 is easy, just plug any USB power supply into the micro-USB port. There’s no power button so the Pi will begin to boot as soon as power is applied, to turn it off, simply shut down the Raspberry Pi3, then remove power. The four built-in USB ports can even output up to 1.2A enabling you to connect more power hungry USB devices (This does require a 2Amp micro USB Power Supply).

On top of all that, the low-level peripherals on the Pi make it great for hardware hacking. The 0.1″ spaced 40-pin GPIO header on the Pi gives you access to 27 GPIO, UART, I2C, SPI as well as 3.3 and 5V sources. Each pin on the GPIO header is identical to its predecessor the Model B+.

blocks.text: The HC-06 is a compact wireless serial interface module designed to enable Bluetooth communication between a microcontroller or embedded system and a master Bluetooth device (such as a smartphone, tablet or PC). It implements a transparent UART-to-Bluetooth link, meaning data transmitted into its RX/TX pins is sent wirelessly and received data is output on the serial pins, simplifying integration.

Engineered as a slave-only Bluetooth module operating under the Bluetooth 2.0 + EDR (Enhanced Data Rate) standard, the HC-06 abstracts away much of the complexity of wireless connectivity. Through simple UART commands and default baud rate (often 9600 bps) the module can pair with a master device, authenticate using a default pass-key (often “1234”) and then forward traffic transparently over the link.

Owing to its small physical size, minimal external components and UART interface, the HC-06 finds wide use in hobby electronics, embedded systems and IoT projects. It draws modest current, uses the 2.4 GHz ISM band (2.402-2.480 GHz), and allows devices without native Bluetooth capability to gain wireless serial connectivity. The simplicity of wiring and communication means it can often be dropped into an existing system with minimal redesign.
Transparent UART interface for wireless serial data exchange.

blocks.text: The USB Type-C 5V 2A Power Bank Module combines lithium battery charging, battery protection, and a 5V boost converter on one compact board. It is suitable for building DIY power banks, portable electronic devices, rechargeable development-board supplies, and battery-powered projects.

The module works with a single 3.7V lithium-ion, 18650, or lithium-polymer battery. It accepts a 5V charging supply through its USB Type-C input and charges the connected battery to the appropriate final voltage. During discharge, the boost converter raises the battery voltage to a regulated 5V output with a maximum rated current of 2A.
Features of the USB Type-C 5V 2A Power Bank Module
The board includes integrated charging management and protection functions. These features help protect the battery against overcharging, excessive discharge, output overcurrent, and short circuits.

Four onboard LED indicators provide an approximate indication of the remaining battery charge. An optional external push button can also be connected to the K control pad for manually activating or deactivating the output and battery indicators.

blocks.text: Solenoid JF-0530B Push-Pull Open Frame Mini Valve Electromagnet

Solenoids are basically electromagnets: they are made of a big coil of copper wire with an armature (a slug of metal) in the middle. When the coil is energized, the slug is pulled into the center of the coil. This makes the solenoid able to pull (from one end) or push (from the other)

This solenoid in particular is fairly small, with a 30mm long body and a ‘captive’ armature with a return spring. This means that when activated with up to 24VDC, the solenoid moves, and then the voltage is removed it springs back to the original position, which is quite handy. Many lower-cost solenoids are only pushed type or only pull type and may not have a captive armature (it’ll fall out!) or don’t have a return spring. This one even has nice mounting tabs, it’s a great all-purpose solenoid.

Solenoids are a great way to induce linear motion for pushing, pulling, or controlling switches and levers. This solenoid is designed to work directly with 24V which makes it a great match for embedded projects. It has a throw of about 10mm and 2 M3 mounting holes on the body.

blocks.text: PT2272-M4 Remote Control Decoder IC DIP-18

The PT2272-M4 is a CMOS remote-control decoder IC designed to pair with PT2262 encoders to receive and decode serial address/data code words. It focuses on reliability and simplicity: address pins accept tri-state settings so systems can use many unique codes, and the device validates incoming frames before enabling outputs. The M4 variant provides four momentary data outputs, making it suitable for small control tasks where each button press should only activate outputs while the signal is present.

Internally the PT2272 decodes 12 AD bits (address + data) followed by a sync bit, compares the decoded address to the pin-set address, and after two consecutive matching frames drives the appropriate data outputs and raises a VT (Valid Transmission) flag. Oscillation timing is set with a single external resistor, so the decoder can be matched to PT2262-based encoders without complex clock circuitry. The momentary output behavior ensures outputs reset automatically when transmissions stop.

Physically the M4 is offered in an 18-pin DIP (300 mil) package and follows standard pinouts for DIN, OSC1/OSC2, VT, VCC and VSS; its operating voltage range and electrical limits make it straightforward to drop into battery-powered or mains-powered remote systems. Typical uses include small home-automation receivers, toys, and garage-type controllers where short, robust remote pulses control actuators.

ram-6231.summary: he IC 74165 is an 8-bit shift register that efficiently stores and transfers data in digital systems, ideal for serial-to-parallel conversion applications.

blocks.text: The 74165 is a high-speed 8-bit parallel-in, serial-out shift register integrated circuit. Its primary function is to convert data from a parallel format into a serial data stream. The device features eight individual parallel data inputs (A through H), which allow an entire byte of data to be loaded into the register simultaneously. This loaded data is then shifted out bit-by-bit through a single serial output pin (QHQH​) upon the application of clock pulses, effectively reducing the number of I/O lines required to read multiple digital signals.

The operation of the 74165 is governed by key control inputs. The Shift/Load (SH/LDSH/LD) input is the master control; setting it low enables the parallel load function, latching the state of the eight data inputs into the internal registers. Setting SH/LDSH/LD high enables the shifting mode. In this mode, data is shifted on the low-to-high transition of the clock, which can be applied to either the Clock (CLKCLK) or the Clock Inhibit (CLKINHCLKINH) pin, as their functions are interchangeable. A high level on CLKINHCLKINH inhibits the clock, pausing the shifting operation.

The device is designed for versatility and ease of use in digital systems. It features a complementary serial output (QH‾QH​​) in addition to the standard output, providing design flexibility. With a wide operating voltage range, it is compatible with various logic levels. Furthermore, multiple 74165 ICs can be easily cascaded by connecting the serial output of one device to the serial input (SERSER) of the next, allowing for the input expansion to 16, 24, or more bits using only a few microcontroller pins.

Frequency: 13.56 MHz, compatible with standard RFID reader modules.
Material: Durable white PVC, blank and ready for printing or labeling.
Read/Write: Fully rewritable memory for custom access codes and data.
Form Factor: Standard 85.6mm x 54mm credit-card size.
These cards are ideal for building custom door access systems, attendance tracking, and RFID-based identification projects with Arduino or Raspberry Pi.
